title: How Long Do HVAC UV Light Bulbs Last?
h1: How Long Do HVAC UV Light Bulbs Last, and When Should You Replace Them?
description: Most HVAC UV bulbs are made to be replaced about once a year, even if they still glow. Here's why output fades, what affects bulb life and what to check.
quick_answer: Most HVAC UV-C bulbs are rated for about 9,000 hours, which is roughly one year of running around the clock. That's why manufacturers usually recommend replacing them every year. The bulb may keep glowing after that, but its germicidal output drops over time, so a lit bulb isn't proof it's still doing its job.
body:
Why do UV bulbs need replacing if they still light up?

UV-C bulbs work by producing ultraviolet light at a wavelength that damages the DNA of mold, bacteria and other microbes. Over time the bulb's ability to produce that light fades, even though it still gives off a visible blue glow.

So the glow you see through the viewing port tells you the bulb has power. It doesn't tell you how much useful UV-C it's putting out. That's why replacement goes by hours or calendar time rather than waiting for the bulb to burn out.

What kinds of HVAC UV lights are there?

  • Coil sterilization lights shine on the evaporator coil and drain pan, where cool, damp conditions let mold and biofilm grow. These usually run 24 hours a day.
  • Air sterilization lights sit in the ductwork or air handler and treat air as it passes. Some are wired to run only when the blower runs.

Both types use similar bulbs, and both follow the manufacturer's replacement schedule. Check the label on your unit or the owner's manual for the exact rating and part number.

What does a UV light actually do for your system?

The evaporator coil stays cold and wet whenever the AC runs. In a dark air handler, that's a good place for mold and slimy biofilm to grow. Growth on the coil can cause musty odors, slow the drain, and coat the fins so less air gets through.

A coil light keeps that surface cleaner between tune-ups. It won't clean a coil that's already caked with dust, and it doesn't catch dust or pollen in the air. That's still the filter's job. Think of the bulb as maintenance for the coil, not a full air cleaner.

What affects how long a UV bulb lasts?

  • Run time: a bulb that's on all the time reaches its rated hours in about a year. One that runs only with the blower may last longer by the calendar.
  • Dust on the bulb: a film of dust blocks UV-C output. A bulb that sits in dirty air works less well, even if it's new.
  • Temperature and airflow: UV-C output changes with air temperature, and very cold air moving over the bulb can lower it.
  • Frequent switching: turning a bulb on and off over and over can wear it faster than steady operation.
  • Bulb quality: an off-brand replacement may not match the original's rating or fit the fixture properly.

How do you know it's time to replace yours?

The most reliable sign is the date. If you don't know when the bulb was last changed, assume it's due. Other clues include:

  • The indicator light on the power supply is out or blinking.
  • You can't see a glow through the viewing window when the light should be on.
  • A musty smell has come back when the AC runs.
  • A technician finds new growth on the coil or drain pan during a tune-up.

Write the install date on a piece of tape near the unit. It saves a lot of guessing next year.

Can I replace an HVAC UV bulb myself?

Some systems are designed for a simple bulb swap, but it's easy to get wrong. UV-C light can injure your eyes and skin, so the power has to be off before the fixture is opened. Bulbs contain a small amount of mercury and need careful handling and proper disposal. Touching the glass leaves skin oils that cut output.

Because the light usually sits inside the air handler in the attic, garage or a hall closet, many homeowners have the bulb changed during their yearly tune-up. That way the technician can also clean the coil and drain pan, check the power supply and confirm the light is aimed where it should be.

Is a UV light worth keeping up?

A UV light works best as one part of a clean-air setup alongside a good filter and a clean coil. In coastal homes where humidity keeps the coil damp, keeping the bulb current helps hold back mold growth. Our indoor air quality team can replace bulbs, check your system and suggest whether a coil or air sterilization light fits your home.
faqs: Should my HVAC UV light be on all the time?

Coil sterilization lights are usually designed to run 24 hours a day so the coil and drain pan stay treated. Some air sterilization lights run only with the blower. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for your model.
Is it safe to look at an HVAC UV light?
No. Don't look directly at a UV-C bulb or open the fixture while it's on. Use the small viewing window, which is designed to block UV-C, to check whether it's lit.
What happens if I don't replace the UV bulb?
Its UV-C output keeps fading, so mold and bacteria can start growing on the coil and drain pan again. The light will still glow, which can make it seem like it's working when it isn't.
How do I dispose of an old UV bulb?
UV bulbs contain a small amount of mercury, so they shouldn't go in household trash. Take them to a household hazardous waste drop-off or ask your technician to take the old bulb away.
How Do You Replace an HVAC UV Light Bulb?

Turn off power to the UV light and the HVAC system, let the lamp cool, then remove the old bulb from its housing without touching the new bulb's glass. Slide in the matching replacement, reconnect it, restore power and confirm it's glowing through the viewing port. Most UV bulbs need replacing about once a year.
Why Do HVAC UV Lights Stop Working?

Most HVAC UV lights stop working because the bulb reached the end of its life, the ballast or power supply failed, a safety switch cut power, or a breaker or connection lost power. A bulb can also keep glowing after it has stopped putting out much UV, so a lit bulb isn't proof it's still working.
